name: getJiraIssue
description: Get a Jira or JSM issue by key or ID. Use for one known issue; use searchJiraIssuesUsingJql to find or list many issues. Reports how many comments an issue has, not the comments themselves — for those use listJiraIssueComments. View "evidence" also returns the issue's links to other issues.

cloudId.description: Site UUID or Jira/Confluence URL for this operation's Atlassian site. cloudId is never silently auto-resolved or reused for you — call getAccessibleAtlassianResources ONCE per session, cache the returned cloudId, and pass it explicitly on this and every subsequent call, since most operations need it. `execute` and its read/write/destructive variants strictly require it for cloudId-scoped operations and fail without it. Not needed for cloudId-less operations (e.g. Bitbucket), which ignore this field.

issueIdOrKey.description: Issue key (PROJ-123), numeric ID, or a Jira issue URL

fields.description: Custom Jira field IDs to fetch (e.g. ["customfield_10010", "customfield_10020"]). Overrides the view's fetch strategy. For custom fields in normal use, prefer view: "evidence", which fetches and maps them automatically. Use ["*all"] to fetch every field (expensive — prefer view: "full" instead).

includeEditableFields.description: When true, also return compact metadata for fields the authenticated user can edit on this issue, including type, allowed values, and operations. Omit unless preparing an edit: this makes an extra Jira REST call.

fieldsByKeys.description: When true, each entry in `fields` is interpreted as a Jira field key (e.g. "summary", "description") instead of a field id. Matches the Jira REST `fieldsByKeys` query parameter. Ignored when `fields` is omitted (default field list uses ids).

expand.description: Additional Jira expand tokens (comma-separated), e.g. "renderedFields,changelog". Merged with any expand the server adds for custom-field mapping (e.g. "names"); duplicate tokens removed. Note "changelog" here returns only the newest page, sorted newest-first, and it accepts startAt/maxResults then ignores them — so it cannot be paged and reports a longer history as complete. Use listJiraIssueChangelogs to read all of it (oldest-first); do not mix their orderings.

properties.description: Issue entity property keys to return (Jira `properties` query param, repeated per key). Omit unless you rely on app-specific issue properties.

failFast.description: When true, forwards Jira's `failFast` query flag for this GET. Omit for Jira default behavior.

responseContentFormat.description: Format for rich-text bodies — description and environment, plus any comment bodies the view returns. Defaults to markdown. Set html to receive HTML, which is lossless, so you can pass it straight back to editJiraIssue/addOrEditJiraIssueComment with contentFormat: html. Bodies holding anything markdown cannot represent — inline media, panels, expands, layouts, statuses, @mentions, dates, emoji — are returned as HTML automatically, because markdown would drop those nodes or turn them into literal text on write-back. An explicit markdown request is overridden for those bodies, with a warning saying so; appliedContentFormat in the response reports the format you actually got.

actionSource.description: Optional invocation attribution. Jira MCP cards set jira_mcp_card; omit for model/tool-loop calls.

view.description: Output view preset. Default: "compact". Options: "compact", "evidence", "full". compact = minimal fields for scanning; evidence = decision-relevant detail; full = complete response.

name: searchJiraIssuesUsingJql
description: Search for Jira issues using JQL, with an optional approximate count. Use view: "evidence" to fetch and map custom fields. Page with nextPageToken until isLast is true. For one known issue, use getJiraIssue. JQL only returns issues; inferring anything else from issue rows is silently incomplete. Use the purpose-built operation for sprints, boards, board config, field history, worklogs, releases, accountIds, issue types, projects and statuses.

cloudId.description: Site UUID or Jira/Confluence URL for this operation's Atlassian site. cloudId is never silently auto-resolved or reused for you — call getAccessibleAtlassianResources ONCE per session, cache the returned cloudId, and pass it explicitly on this and every subsequent call, since most operations need it. `execute` and its read/write/destructive variants strictly require it for cloudId-scoped operations and fail without it. Not needed for cloudId-less operations (e.g. Bitbucket), which ignore this field.

jql.description: JQL query string e.g. "project = PROJ AND status = 'In Progress'". If the tool returns a repairHint, follow it and retry.

searchResultMode.description: Default "issues". Never count for normal search or if nextPageToken used. If total for same query is known, reuse it. Use "count" only when no trusted count exists and either the user asks or a downstream step needs it. Use "all" only if both count and issues required.

fields.description: Fields per issue (e.g. ["summary", "status", "customfield_10010"]). customfield_* IDs are site-specific — discover the correct id for story points etc. on this Cloud site. Honoured exactly when supplied. Values map to issues[].fields.customFields (human labels), not raw customfield_* keys. The default "compact" view omits custom fields; use view: "evidence" for velocity/sprint JQL (fetches and maps all custom fields) or pass explicit customfield_* IDs.

nextPageToken.description: Pagination token from a previous response to fetch the next page

responseContentFormat.description: Format for rich-text bodies (description, environment, comments) when the view returns them. Defaults to markdown; html is lossless for a later editJiraIssue. Issues holding anything markdown cannot represent (media, panels, expands, statuses, @mentions) are returned as HTML automatically, decided per issue. An explicit markdown request is overridden for those bodies, with a warning saying so; appliedContentFormat in the response reports the format you actually got.

actionSource.description: Optional invocation attribution. Jira MCP cards set jira_mcp_card; omit for model/tool-loop calls.

view.description: Output view preset. Default: "compact". Options: "compact", "evidence", "full". compact = minimal fields for scanning; evidence = decision-relevant detail; full = complete response.

name: createJiraIssue
description: Create a new Jira issue. Put custom fields in additional_fields, keyed by field name or customfield_* ID; values are resolved automatically, so no field lookup is needed first. A rejected create returns the required fields and their allowed values, so retry from that.

cloudId.description: Site UUID or Jira/Confluence URL for this operation's Atlassian site. cloudId is never silently auto-resolved or reused for you — call getAccessibleAtlassianResources ONCE per session, cache the returned cloudId, and pass it explicitly on this and every subsequent call, since most operations need it. `execute` and its read/write/destructive variants strictly require it for cloudId-scoped operations and fail without it. Not needed for cloudId-less operations (e.g. Bitbucket), which ignore this field.

issueType.description: Issue type name (e.g. Bug, Task, Story, Epic). Use listJiraProjectIssueTypesMetadata to list valid types for this project if unsure.

description.description: Issue description in markdown, or HTML with contentFormat html. Converted to Jira ADF automatically.

contentFormat.description: Body format for description. Defaults to markdown; html adds panels, tables and status lozenges. For HTML body shapes, first get the format guide via the generic operation runner (execute) as name=getContentFormatGuide, inputs={toolName: "createJiraIssue"}. Inline media needs an existing issue: create first, then embed with editJiraIssue. When the HTML content-format feature is disabled the call is rejected rather than downgraded, because markdown would store the HTML tags as literal text.

priority.description: Priority name (e.g. High, Medium, Low, Highest, Lowest).

assignee.description: Account ID of the assignee. Resolve a name with listJiraIssueAssignableUsers, which returns only users who can be assigned in this project; lookupJiraAccountId resolves any user and does not check that.

parent.description: Parent issue key for sub-tasks or child issues (e.g. PROJ-10).

additional_fields.description:
Additional Jira fields. Keys can be human-readable field names or raw customfield_* IDs. Values can be human-readable (resolved automatically) or already-correct Jira shapes. Examples:
  {"Story Points": 8}                          ← number field by name
  {"Team": "Backend"}                          ← option/select by name
  {"Reviewers": ["alice@acme.com", "bob@acme.com"]}  ← multi-user by accountId
  {"Component Area": "Platform / Auth"}        ← cascading select as "Parent / Child"
  {"customfield_10010": 8}                     ← raw ID (no resolution needed, fastest)
  {"components": [{"name": "Backend"}]}        ← system array field (raw shape)
  {"fixVersions": [{"name": "v2.0"}]}          ← system array field (raw shape)
On error, the response includes allowedValues and a repairHint for self-correction.

assignToSprint.description: Optional sprint assignment after the issue is created. Accepts a numeric sprint ID, an exact sprint name, or "active" to resolve an active sprint. Numeric sprint IDs assign directly and do not need board lookup. When omitted, createJiraIssue behaves exactly as before and does not make sprint calls.

name: addOrEditJiraIssueComment
description: Add a comment to a Jira issue, or edit an existing comment. Omit commentId to add a new comment; provide commentId to edit that comment. Comment text (commentBody) supports markdown. To edit, first get the commentId from listJiraIssueComments. Returns the commentId needed to edit or delete it later, plus — unless inline media was embedded — the stored body and appliedContentFormat, the format it was written in.

cloudId.description: Site UUID or Jira/Confluence URL for this operation's Atlassian site. cloudId is never silently auto-resolved or reused for you — call getAccessibleAtlassianResources ONCE per session, cache the returned cloudId, and pass it explicitly on this and every subsequent call, since most operations need it. `execute` and its read/write/destructive variants strictly require it for cloudId-scoped operations and fail without it. Not needed for cloudId-less operations (e.g. Bitbucket), which ignore this field.

issueIdOrKey.description: Issue key (e.g. PROJ-123) or a Jira issue URL

commentBody.description: Comment text. Markdown by default; set contentFormat: html to pass HTML instead. Required unless adding a new comment purely to embed a file via inlineFileId. Editing replaces the whole comment body: pass the full intended text (fetch the current comment first to preserve it), or "" for media only. Editing a body that already contains inline media must use contentFormat: html — markdown drops it. For HTML body shapes (inline media, panels, tables), first get the format guide via the generic operation runner (execute) as name=getContentFormatGuide, inputs={toolName: "addOrEditJiraIssueComment"}.

contentFormat.description: Body format for commentBody. Defaults to markdown. html preserves inline media across a read-modify-write; a body fetched as HTML can be written straight back (Jira resolves media collection/filename server-side and omits them on read — not data loss). Requires the HTML content-format feature; when it is disabled the call is rejected rather than downgraded, because markdown would store the HTML tags as literal text and drop the media.

commentVisibility.description:
Restrict comment visibility to a Jira group or role. Shape: `{"type":"group"|"role","value":"<name>"}`.
Role and group names are site-specific, so do not reuse a name from another site.
On JSM this does not make a comment internal — a restricted comment stays customer-visible
(`jsdPublic: true`). Use `jsmCommentType: "internalNote"` for that.

jsmCommentType.description: JSM comment type. Use internalNote for an internal note or publicComment for a customer-visible comment. Applies when adding or editing a JSM comment. Omit for existing Jira behavior.

commentId.description: ID of an existing comment to edit. When omitted, a new comment is added.

inlineFileId.description: Media file ID(s) from uploadAttachmentToJiraIssue to append inline to the comment, e.g. ["id1","id2"]. Requires contentFormat: html and a matching inlineFileCollection (paired by index). Appends at the end; for exact placement, author the media node in the HTML commentBody instead. A file already embedded in the body is rejected (would duplicate).

inlineFileCollection.description: Media collection(s) from the upload step, paired to inlineFileId by index (a single value applies to all). Required whenever inlineFileId is set.

inlineFileName.description: Optional file name(s) (from the upload step's fileName), paired to inlineFileId by index. Only selects the render shape: images render as a block image, other files as an inline chip. Omit to default to the image shape.

responseContentFormat.description: Format of the echoed comment body. Defaults to the format written, so an html write reads back as html. Bodies markdown cannot represent (media, panels, statuses, @mentions) are always echoed as HTML so a follow-up edit does not destroy them. An explicit markdown request is overridden for those bodies, with a warning saying so; appliedContentFormat in the response reports the format you actually got.

name: executeRead
description:
Run a read-only Atlassian operation by name across all Atlassian products.
Only use an operation name from discover results or one already in your tool list; never guess, assume, or invent a name — when unsure, call discover first.
If the user provides a Jira/Confluence URL, pass it directly as cloudId — no need to call getAccessibleAtlassianResources.
Pass all inputs as a flat object — the server routes each to the right location (path, query, or body) automatically.
Use responseFields for field filtering, e.g. ["key","fields.summary","fields.status.name"].
Use view to select a named output preset (e.g. "compact", "evidence", "full") when the operation supports views.

cloudId.description: Site UUID or Jira/Confluence URL for this operation's Atlassian site. cloudId is never silently auto-resolved or reused for you — call getAccessibleAtlassianResources ONCE per session, cache the returned cloudId, and pass it explicitly on this and every subsequent call, since most operations need it. `execute` and its read/write/destructive variants strictly require it for cloudId-scoped operations and fail without it. Not needed for cloudId-less operations (e.g. Bitbucket), which ignore this field.

name.description: Operation name to run. Only use an operation name from discover results or one already in your tool list; never guess, assume, or invent a name — when unsure, call discover first.

inputs.description: Flat input object — pass all parameters here. The server routes each to path, query, or body automatically.

responseFields.description: Dot-notation fields to return, e.g. ["key","fields.summary"]. Filters response.

view.description: Named output view preset (e.g. "compact", "evidence", "full"). Only applies when the operation declares views. Overridden by responseFields if both are supplied.
